$comment: Policy for the extended MCP tool families (routes/mcp-tools/*.js). Same stance as the other policy files: this JSON is the enforcement source of truth, the tool descriptions only summarize it. Cross-cutting contract on every new write: dry_run previews without touching anything; expected_sha256 guards any file edit; anything destructive takes a snapshot/export FIRST and demands a one-time confirmation_token issued by the tool itself; the server writes the mcp_ledger row and the audit entry (and, for project-scoped writes, the hash-chained change record) — the caller never does.

feature_flags.$comment: Read through app_settings (feature_flag:<name>), defaults below. list_feature_flags / set_feature_flag manage them; a flipped flag takes effect on the next call.

mcp.builds.description: start_project_build, approve_design, run_checklist, run_interview answers — the verbs that spend a project's model budget.

mcp.destructive.description: Every delete / restore / rollback / reboot verb. Off = those tools refuse before issuing a confirmation token.

mcp.host_control.description: host_service_control, install_package, reboot_host, host snapshots, restore_proxypilot_db.

mcp.self_edit.description: The self-editing family (still requires a key minted with scope.self_edit).

mcp.security_scans.description: run_lynis / run_trivy (host binaries must be installed).

mcp.dns.description: Cloudflare DNS record tools (need the DNS-01 Cloudflare token).

mcp.webhooks.description: Outbound webhook notifications (list_webhooks / set_webhook and their dispatch).

mcp.storage.description: The storage family's mutating verbs (create_zpool, datasets, snapshots, replace_disk, scrub, import/export, the Incus binding, sanoid/syncoid policy and replication). destroy_dataset, zfs_rollback, destroy_zfs_snapshot and rollback_guest_dataset are additionally behind mcp.destructive. Readers (list_disks, zpool_status, zfs_list, …) are never gated.

mcp.migration.description: The migration family's mutating verbs (create_migration, approve_migration, migration_cutover, cancel_migration). Turning it off leaves the readers (get_migration, list_migrations) working and stops any new migration token from being minted.

mcp.platform.description: The platform family (Platform Setup / Full Platform): the readers (get_platform_setup, get_platform_service, list_platform_jobs, get_platform_job, platform_preflight) and the writes (save_platform_setup, apply_platform_setup, continue_platform_setup). manage_platform_service and reset_platform_setup are additionally behind mcp.destructive.

mcp.platform.purge.description: reset_platform_setup with purge_data: true — deletes the owned platform data (directories, volumes, networks, protected credential rows) after a verified backup set. OFF by default; without it a reset keeps all data.

platform.$comment: Platform Setup over MCP (routes/mcp-tools/platform.js). Every tool calls the dashboard's own store functions; the tools below are the whole surface. Runtime actions and reset use the one-time confirmation_token bound to the review digest they previewed; reset's purge backup set is written under exports_dir/platform-reset-<job id> and verified before any deletion. The human_only actions are step-up-gated in the dashboard and have NO MCP tool — get_platform_setup.next_actions points the person at them.
human_only: permanent master login for bootstrap retirement
any secret input: client secrets, admin tokens, the Infisical personal password, PGP material, unseal shares, root/bootstrap token

migration.$comment: Adopting a source host (lib/migration). The agent holds ONE single-use, scoped, expiring token and pins TLS to this ProxyPilot's certificate. The inventory manifest carries .env PATHS and KEY NAMES only — the server REFUSES a manifest that carries a value, so a tampered agent cannot put a secret in the database. Nothing is copied until an operator approves the inventory; the imported guest comes up with the default-deny egress fence and no route.

transports.incus-migrate: whole-machine: wraps the official incus-migrate with a server-supplied answer script and a single-use Incus trust token
transports.rootfs-tar: whole-machine on a Proxmox/nested LXC, where incus-migrate cannot run inside the guest: tar the rootfs, PUT it here, import it as a split image
transports.rsync: application mode: the app directories plus a logical database dump restored inside the new guest

never: read or transmit the VALUE of an environment variable, a database password or a private key
start copying before an operator approved the inventory (unless auto_transfer was explicitly set)
publish a route or lift the egress fence on an imported guest as part of the import

storage.$comment: ZFS storage management (lib/storage). Devices are addressed by /dev/disk/by-id only; the OS device (backing / and /boot, resolved through findmnt + lsblk holders) is refused with no override; a mounted device, an md/LVM/LUKS holder, or a member of an imported pool is refused too; any other signature needs wipe: true. Every mutation is plan/confirm: dry_run returns the plan and its sha256 token, the real call carries confirm + token, a changed plan invalidates it. The managed layout is <pool>/incus (Incus storage pool source), <pool>/backups, <pool>/exports.

install.$comment: install_storage_toolchain runs the checkout's scripts/install-storage.sh through the ROOT update runner (deploy/proxypilot-update.service), the same privilege path as a self-update. The caller supplies nothing: the action name is fixed, flags are refused, and the script path is resolved from the runner's recorded source-dir, never from the request. It installs packages, systemd units and helper scripts and touches no block device. storage_preflight must pass its blocking checks first.

explicitly_absent.mdadm_under_zfs: Never: create_zpool takes whole disks only and refuses active md members.
explicitly_absent.zpool_destroy: Not offered: export_pool is the reversible verb; destroying a pool stays a hands-on host operation.

self_edit.note: Patches land in the candidate clone, never in the live checkout. promote_self fast-forwards the live checkout to the candidate HEAD (recording the previous HEAD) and requests the root update runner with --rebuild; rollback_self resets the live checkout to the recorded HEAD and requests the same rebuild. Both refuse when the live checkout is dirty, when an update is live, or when the host agent is unreachable.

host_services.$comment: Units host_service_control may touch, with the verbs allowed on each. docker and ssh are deliberately restart/status-only: stopping docker kills this backend, stopping ssh locks the operator out.

guest_services.$comment: service_control inside a guest: any unit, these verbs. status/is-active are read-only; the rest confirm-gated.

apt_packages.$comment: install_package inside a guest: only these Debian/Ubuntu package names, non-interactive apt-get. Extend here, never on the wire.

lxc_devices.$comment: add_lxc_device: disk sources must live under one of these host roots (a guest must never mount /etc, /root or another guest's rootfs); proxy devices listen on the host at tcp/udp:0.0.0.0:<port> only.

settings.$comment: get_settings / set_setting: the app_settings keys an MCP client may read and write. Secret-bearing keys are readable as '[set]' / '[unset]' only and never writable here. exports.compression (zstd | gzip | none, default zstd) is the compressor every guest export, prepared download and S3 snapshot push uses; it falls back to gzip on a host without the zstd binary.

route_options.$comment: set_route_options: which keys render. rate_limit needs the http.handlers.rate_limit Caddy module (caddy-ratelimit); the tool checks caddy list-modules and refuses with the install hint when it is absent.

explicitly_absent.force_delete_without_snapshot: delete_lxc_container refuses unless the guest has at least one snapshot AND an export tarball was taken (export: false is an explicit opt-out that the ledger records).
explicitly_absent.unscoped_self_edit: No key edits ProxyPilot itself unless it was minted with scope.self_edit — including the operator's original full-access key.
explicitly_absent.discard_local: promote_self / rollback_self never pass --discard-local and refuse on a dirty live checkout, same as run_proxypilot_update.
